bluf: Rankings.io is a US, founder led, search first law firm marketing agency built around personal injury, claiming 300+ PI firms helped to over 100K high value cases and nine straight years on the Inc. 5000 from 2018 to 2026. It is doing what a legal SEO shop does at dusk on the Solar Arc: selling GEO and AI SEO to get firms named in ChatGPT, Perplexity and AI Overviews, plus ChatGPT Ads and LSAs. Where it is going is the same PI playbook applied to criminal, family, immigration and other practices. A rival should know that its robots.txt blocks GPTBot, ClaudeBot and two more AI crawlers while it sells AI visibility, and that 15 of its 16 named clients carry no described work.
doing:
Rankings.io positions as a search first law firm marketing agency built around personal injury, applying its PI playbook to criminal, family, immigration and other high value practices: it ranks law firms in Google and now in AI answers, and sells the rest of the funnel around that. The headline claim is 300+ personal injury firms helped to generate over 100K high value cases; the prominence signals add nine straight Inc. 5000 years (2018 to 2026), a vote into the top 1% of digital agencies for attorneys and a 4.9 average client review rating, all claims on its own pages.

The sold mix leads with SEO, scored 3: the meta pitches the agency for law firms that dominate search, and SEO leads the services and the case studies. Five core lines score 2. AI Search / GEO rests on dedicated AI SEO and GEO pages, an AIO nav item and an AI SEO/GEO PI case study. Creator & Influencer rests on an Organic Social Media service backed by four organic social case studies including LinkedIn and Instagram growth. Local rests on a Local Services Ads page and a metro focused local SEO section. Paid Search rests on Google Search Ads, PPC and LSA services and a Google Ads PI ROI case study. Web & Product rests on a Website Design service for fast WordPress law firm sites and a 14 site portfolio. Content and paid social score 1; data and measurement, CRO, email, AI automation, B2B, programmatic and retail media score 0. The service list adds ChatGPT Ads, Paid Digital and Mass Torts Marketing; proprietary lines are the Search Dominance Engine and The Attorney Rankings System; no partners are listed.

Its AI posture carries its own contradiction: it sells GEO and AI SEO to get firms named in ChatGPT, Perplexity and AI Overviews, plus ChatGPT Ads, while its robots.txt blocks AI crawlers. The one dated move is the 2026 ninth consecutive Inc. 5000 listing. Pricing signals: month to month terms with no long contracts, clients keep ownership of ad accounts, creative and data, and a free growth audit as the entry point; no price shows. The record lists no news, case study text or jobs. Conspicuously absent: any data or measurement line for an agency that sells signed cases, an office list, a founding year and a headcount.
clients:
The client type is mid market and the verticals are personal injury law, criminal defense, family law, immigration law, employment law, bankruptcy, estate planning and probate, and mass torts; the home market is the US, with no office listed.

The needs read holds 16 clients, 1 with an observed need and 15 named only, all 16 from case study or portfolio slugs. The one observed is Cowen Rodriguez Peacock, coded organic demand and social and creators on an organic social results slug. The case study slugs name Galine, Frye, Fitting & Frangos, Ronald Weiss Law Firm, Emroch & Kilduff, Gomez Trial Attorneys, The Levin Firm and Dolman Law Group with nothing about the work; the portfolio slugs name Ed Bernstein & Associates, Rawlins Law, The Reinartz Law Firm, The Bruning Law Firm, Holliday Karatinos Law Firm, Abels & Annes, P.C., Morris Law LLC, Fletcher Injury Law and Nicolet Law, which by their placement in a website portfolio are inferred as web build and platform, and otherwise as organic demand from the SEO lead. Against a claim of 300+ PI firms helped, a record of 16 slugs and one described result is the finding: the volume is asserted, the work is not shown.

One client is shared: The Levin Firm also sits on the book of consultwebs.

What the base needs next: PI and other contingency practices sit under KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation), the judgment the Horus read marks Rankings.io best placed for, and KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out), its most exposed through SEO and paid search. It is very likely, high confidence, that these firms will ask to be named in AI answers before they ask about rankings, which is what the AIO line and the LinkedIn ebook ad sell; it is likely, moderate confidence, that they will press on price for the SEO and web hours, given displacement 69.4 on the Monsoon read.
house: Say and do: four lines tested, three practised, integrity 75. AI search is contradicted: it sells AI visibility and its robots.txt blocks GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot and Google-Extended, with 6 AI topic URLs in its sitemap and no llms.txt reading on record. Paid search is corroborated: 63 Google ads in the Transparency Center, 2 in the last 30 days, 57 text, under Rankings.io, LLC, last shown 2026-09-27, with no sample text on record. Creator and influencer is corroborated by its own Instagram and YouTube channels. Publishing cadence is recorded as corroborated on 0 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days and 350 in 365, from 987 URLs: a year of output and a quiet quarter. LinkedIn shows 24+ company page ads, a floor against 87 name matches, one reading 'The math is simple. Better visibility = more signed cases' and another 'Volume isn't the goal. Profitability is.' The tag stack is GTM and Dealfront Leadfeeder on WordPress, with Leadfeeder the one ABM tool; no social pixels, no test tools. The one flagged gap is the crawler block.
market:
Horus puts Rankings.io at tailwind index 5.3, band Neutral, percentile 30, 16:35 on the Solar Arc, dusk (Atum). Best placed for KJ1 (the click replaced by the citation, driven by AI Search / GEO) and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers). Most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle hollowed out, driven by SEO, Paid Search and Paid Social) and KJ4 (the platforms absorbing the execution layer). Best scenario fit: The Toll Road at 40/100. It is making P3 (Local Services Ads work is evidenced), partial on P1 (no audited AI visibility product), P4 (paid media without first party data, creative volume or measurement depth) and P8 (talks ads inside assistants with no holdout capability), absent on P2, P6 and P7; P5 is unknown.

The Monsoon read is 66.9, band Onshore wind, percentile 87: migration 64.4 against displacement 69.4, so clients leaving on price edges ahead of hours moving with the agency. The sold mix supplies 64 of the index, SEO (18) and Web & Product (12) carrying the most movable hours; the work would go 65% to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America. The footprint is inferred: no hub offices, no onshore claims, mid market client type adding 5 points.
openings:
The strongest opening is the crawler contradiction: it sells GEO and AI SEO to get law firms named in ChatGPT, Perplexity and AI Overviews and blocks GPTBot, ClaudeBot and the rest on its own robots.txt. A rival that shows a prospect the block and its own open house can very likely (high confidence) win the AI visibility conversation with any PI firm weighing the two. Falsifier: a later compile showing the crawlers unblocked or an llms.txt published closes it.

The Levin Firm already sits with consultwebs and is the account to contest first. The book is thin: 15 of 16 named clients carry no described work against a claim of 300+ firms, so ask any of the portfolio firms what was done beyond the website. Displacement 69.4 says the mid market legal book buys on price and SEO and web carry the movable hours, so an offshore delivered SEO and build offer undercuts the retainers; month to month terms with no long contracts make the switch cheap. It sells no data or measurement line while selling signed cases: a rival with intake and case value attribution offers the proof it cannot. No audited AI visibility product (P1 partial), no feed, schema or entity work (P2 absent) and no public price (P5 unknown) round it out; the idle sitemap (0 updates in 90 days) is the symptom to raise.
watch: I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, October 2026: output or outcome pricing at a top five holdco would sharpen the KJ6 exposure of a month to month agency with no public price.

I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, late October 2026: growth below 10% flags cannibalization of the SEO lead, above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and the KJ1 tailwind its AIO line sells into.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.

I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the $2B milestone and pricing below $20 CPM decide whether the ChatGPT Ads it lists become a channel it can prove without holdouts (P8 partial).
The robots.txt block on GPTBot, ClaudeBot and the others: whether the next compile finds it lifted is the single change that would close the strongest opening.
The next Radar compile: this dossier is only as fresh as the 2026-09-28 compile; Google ads last shown 2026-09-27 and 0 sitemap updates in 90 days after 350 in the year.
